svg.aria-label: How to write г: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing г
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of г (cyrillic), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase г demonstration, 01:54–01:57, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source note on variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:54–01:57 lowercase г demonstration, the pen rises from the baseline into the main shoulder, descends and turns at the baseline, then continues through a smaller rising-and-falling exit arch in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a rounded cursive form with two humps; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a block-like printed form with one straight upright and a top bar, and has no exit arch. This learner path preserves the source's baseline-to-shoulder-to-baseline lift count while fitting the printed form: climb the upright, sweep right along the top bar, reverse to the junction, and descend the upright without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's smaller exit arch, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant both humps differently.
